outcome: abnormal lateralization (long-range underconnectivity, left-over-right qEEG functional connectivity ratio, short-range overconnectivity)
cohort: The study included children and adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) possessing retained primitive reflexes (RPRs) and a control group without RPRs, with some receiving an intervention.
finding: Clinical improvement and the absence of retained primitive reflexes may be linked to variations in qEEG frequency bands and more optimized brain networks, leading to more developmentally appropriate long-range connectivity links, primarily in the right hemisphere.
